newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST MAYOR ENLISTS U.S. HELP AGAINST CRIME WAVE.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST MAYOR ENLISTS U.S. HELP AGAINST CRIME WAVE.

text.p: Former New York police commissioner William J Bratton arrived in Budapest on Wednesday at the invitation of Mayor Gabor Demszky, to help stem a crime wave that saw six bombings causing two fatalities this year.
Both host and guest acknowledged the organisational and legislative differences between the two police forces but Bratton said a substantial part of his U.S. experience is relevant for Hungary.
"Quite a lot," he told Reuters. "Like identifying and eliminating the sources of crime".
Demszky said that during his 1995 visit he was impressed by the results New York has achieved in curbing crime.

In Budapest, at least three people have been killed and almost two dozen car showrooms, restaurants, pubs, nightclubs or peep shows have been damaged since September by hand grenades or petrol-filled bombs.
Budapest's recently appointed police chief, Attila Berta said earlier he expected further attacks linked to what he called a "mafia war associated with the development of society".
Demszky said the key to better public safety is improving cooperation between police, politics and the public.
"The view to instantly blame police for the crime situation needs to be changed, but this will take time," he said.
Demszky said his move to call for outside advice was also a gesture towards fellow Free Democrat politician and Minister of Interior Gabor Kuncze.
"This should be enormous help for him," he said.
Kuncze sacked Hungary's four top police leaders last November and said at the time he trusted the new national police chief to be able to produce quick results.
Hungarian police has not yet achieved a breakthrough in the bombing series many believe to be related with gang turf wars.
